title: Blender MCP and The Future Of Creative Tools - Siddharth Ahuja
talk_summary: The speaker built Blender MCP, letting an LLM client drive Blender via a lean set of MCP tools plus script execution, and shows rapid scene/game/asset generation. The main transferable lessons are tool-surface minimalism, letting the model write code against a scripting API instead of exposing many narrow tools, and treating the client as an orchestrator across external APIs.

takeaways.technique: Minimize and differentiate MCP tool surface
takeaways.what_they_do: They refactored the MCP repeatedly because ~14-15 tools confused the model; they kept the toolset lean and made each tool clearly distinct so the model picks correctly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I had about I think 14 or 15 tools and it kept getting confused on what to use
takeaways.numbers: 14-15 tools caused confusion; refactored multiple times

takeaways.technique: Expose a scripting/execution tool instead of many narrow tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Because Blender can execute code, the LLM writes scripts to accomplish modeling, asset import, and node setup rather than needing a dedicated tool per operation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a tool with scripting can remove a lot of the heavy lifting

takeaways.technique: Client-as-orchestrator across external APIs and local tools
takeaways.what_they_do: The LLM client orchestrates between local tools (Blender) and external asset APIs, choosing which to call to satisfy a high-level intent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the client is kind of the orchestrator

takeaways.technique: Keep the interface lean; resist feature bloat
takeaways.what_they_do: They attribute the tool's success to staying lean and generalist rather than adding every possible feature.
takeaways.evidence_quote: don't bloat the UX just because you can

takeaways.what_they_do: They note the same MCP got ~3x better when a newer model shipped, implying capability is model-bound and worth re-evaluating.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Gemini 2.5 came out and that made it already 3x better
takeaways.numbers: ~3x improvement attributed to a model upgrade
